title: Probing the Origins of 1,800 MHz Radio Frequency Electromagnetic Radiation Induced Damage in Mouse Immortalized Germ Cells and Spermatozoa in vitro
authors: Houston Brendan J.; Nixon Brett; King Bruce V.; Aitken R. John; De Iuliis Geoffry N.
integrity_status: Exact held source PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Cultured mouse germ-cell models and isolated mature mouse sperm under a continuous-wave laboratory exposure, without exposed men or reproductive-success outcomes.
limitations: Small biological replication, many connected comparisons and mixed stage/time/assay patterns constrain interpretation. No human clinical fertility outcome or safe-use threshold was tested. Scientific, numerical and human review remain pending.
citation: Houston Brendan J.; Nixon Brett; King Bruce V.; Aitken R. John; De Iuliis Geoffry N.. Probing the Origins of 1,800 MHz Radio Frequency Electromagnetic Radiation Induced Damage in Mouse Immortalized Germ Cells and Spermatozoa in vitro 2018. DOI: 10.3389/fpubh.2018.00270.

claims.text: The experiment found stage-, time- and assay-dependent responses. Mature sperm showed selected later motility and oxidative-DNA findings, while fragmentation results differed by assay and exposure interval.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 8 to 9 and 13 to 14, Results, Figures and Discussion

claims.text: Mitochondrial probe signals and selected sperm assays do not establish a complete causal disease pathway or human infertility. The experiment studied isolated cells and sperm rather than conception or offspring outcomes.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 5, Methods; pages 13 to 15, Discussion

title: RF-EMF Exposure near 5G NR Small Cells
authors: Aerts Sam; Deprez Kenneth; Verloock Leen; Olsen Robert G.; Martens Luc; Tran Phung; Joseph Wout
integrity_status: Exact held source PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Limited Belgian base-station measurements rescaled to small-cell powers and combined with modeled traffic/user scenarios; physical exposure study, not a clinical cohort.
limitations: Limited sites and modeled inputs do not establish representative personal exposure or lifetime health outcomes. Close-distance coverage and nearby maximum labels require clarification; numerical release, scientific appraisal and human review remain pending.
citation: Aerts Sam; Deprez Kenneth; Verloock Leen; Olsen Robert G.; Martens Luc; Tran Phung; Joseph Wout. RF-EMF Exposure near 5G NR Small Cells 2023. DOI: 10.3390/s23063145.

claims.text: The measured base stations did not themselves meet the paper's small-cell power definitions. Measurements were rescaled to selected small-cell settings, and typical-user and non-user scenarios were calculated rather than directly sampled as population exposure.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical page 6, site definitions; pages 10 to 12, scenario interpretation and Discussion

claims.text: The reported rescaled scenarios were below the reference levels used under the stated assumptions. Antenna geometry, traffic, close-distance gaps and unresolved maximum-label wording limit numerical reuse; no health outcomes were measured.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 9 to 12, Figures, Table and Discussion

title: Exposure to 26.5 GHz, 5G modulated and unmodulated signal, does not affect key cellular endpoints of human neuroblastoma cells
authors: Sannino Anna; Allocca Mariateresa; Scarfì Maria Rosaria; Romeo Stefania; Peluso Valentina; Panariello Gaetano; Schettino Fulvio; Chirico Gaetano; Zeni Olga
integrity_status: Exact held source PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Human neuroblastoma-cell cultures under specified modulated and continuous-wave high-band laboratory signals, including a later menadione challenge.
limitations: Few independent experiments, a single cell model and specified timing limit transfer to human disease. Methods and figure wording differ on repeated measurements; raw-data reconciliation, numerical release, scientific and human review remain pending.
citation: Sannino Anna; Allocca Mariateresa; Scarfì Maria Rosaria; Romeo Stefania; Peluso Valentina; Panariello Gaetano; Schettino Fulvio; Chirico Gaetano; Zeni Olga. Exposure to 26.5 GHz, 5G modulated and unmodulated signal, does not affect key cellular endpoints of human neuroblastoma cells 2025. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-025-04834-3.

claims.text: Neither tested signal significantly changed the measured cell-cycle distribution or comet-assay damage relative to sham. Prior RF exposure also did not significantly alter the damage response to the later menadione challenge.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 to 9, Results and Figures

claims.text: A delayed chemical challenge in a transformed cell line does not represent every combined exposure or human tissue dose. Nonsignificant comparisons under this protocol do not establish universal equivalence or absence of clinical harm.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 3 to 6, experimental sequence; pages 9 to 10, Discussion and Conclusion

title: Moderate Dose of Trolox Preventing the Deleterious Effects of Wi-Fi Radiation on Spermatozoa In vitro through Reduction of Oxidative Stress Damage
authors: Ding Shang-Shu; Sun Ping; Zhang Zhou; Liu Xiang; Tian Hong; Huo Yong-Wei; Wang Li-Rong; Han Yan; Xing Jun-Ping
integrity_status: Exact held source PDF/native identity matched; selected passages freshly inspected; no scientific, numerical or human approval asserted
scope: Split-sample isolated human semen under a Wi-Fi-labelled laboratory arrangement with exposed Trolox conditions; no oral intervention or reproductive-success follow-up.
limitations: Incomplete exposure verification, absent compound-only comparators and uncertain paired/repeated analysis constrain causal interpretation. Culture concentrations are not oral supplement doses. Scientific, numerical and human review remain pending.
citation: Ding Shang-Shu; Sun Ping; Zhang Zhou; Liu Xiang; Tian Hong; Huo Yong-Wei; Wang Li-Rong; Han Yan; Xing Jun-Ping. Moderate Dose of Trolox Preventing the Deleterious Effects of Wi-Fi Radiation on Spermatozoa In vitro through Reduction of Oxidative Stress Damage 2018. DOI: 10.4103/0366-6999.225045.

claims.text: Trolox attenuation was selective rather than uniform across the sperm and molecular assays. Mitochondrial measures were not rescued, and a higher concentration was not uniformly more favorable.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 4 to 10, Results, Figures and Discussion

claims.text: The authors state that precise exposure could not be verified with the available equipment. Missing unexposed compound-only controls and unclear paired/repeated-measure handling limit attribution, and the experiment does not establish clinical supplement prevention or infertility risk.
claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Methods; pages 9 to 10, Discussion and limitations

claims.text: Reported calling, streaming and gaming behavior is not measured absorbed RF dose. Wi-Fi was not carried into the longitudinal models because the exposure categories had too little contrast; this is not a strong longitudinal router-exposure test.
